The Build Guide

Everything needed to finish the TradeSura app, screen by screen. For Oliver, from Matt. This is version 2 — it replaces the Master Build Doc v1 and every earlier fix list. Where an older document says something different, this one wins.

Part 0 — Read this first

What TradeSura is, in three sentences. A gas engineer builds his own monthly care plan in the app (say £12 a month), offers it to the customer at the end of a job, and the customer signs up on their phone with a Direct Debit. TradeSura collects the money, keeps 20%, and pays the engineer his 80% every Friday. The app's whole job is to make offering a plan take under 90 seconds.

How this guide works. Each part covers one area of the app. Most parts open with a picture — the target design. Build the screen to match the picture. Underneath each picture are the rules that the picture can't show (what happens on tap, what changes with state, what the maths is). A few strings differ from what's printed in a picture — those corrections are listed in Part 18, and where a picture and this text disagree, the text wins.

The tags used throughout:

  • P0 Do first — these block everything else.
  • LAW A standing rule of the product. Never break one to close a ticket — if a rule and a ticket collide, flag it to Matt instead.
  • CONFIG Matt hasn't made the final call. Build the mechanism so either answer works — don't hardcode one.
  • NOTE A picture-vs-build difference. The pictures were AI-generated and carry a few cosmetic slips — these tell you what to build instead.

The finish line is one walk on Matt's phone, end to end, described in Part 20. Everything in this guide serves that walk.

Part 1 — Do these three things first

P0 1.1  Build the plan room — it doesn't exist yet

The biggest finding of the app walk: there is no way to create a plan anywhere in the app. Not in setup, not behind My plans. Nothing downstream (offers, checkout, payouts, gates) can work until it exists. So the first job is to build:

  • The create-a-plan wizard — four steps, spec in Part 8.
  • The My plans page — the room where plans live, spec in Part 7.
  • The plan editor with versioning — spec in Part 7.
  • Then wire five doors to that one room: the Getting Started hub's "Build my plan" · the dashboard quick action "My plans" · the Account row "My plans" · the "Manage plans" link inside the Add customer sheet · the offer gate's "Build my plan →" button.

P0 1.2  Wire the Getting Started hub

The hub's buttons are painted doors — "Build my plan", "Import customers" and "Send my pack" do nothing (only Stripe's "Set up payments" and "Skip setup for now" work). It's one routing job: Build my plan → the new wizard · Import customers → the Customers import flow · Send my pack → address capture + pack order queue (Part 17). Details in Part 5.

P0 1.3  The phantom customer — tell Matt which bug it is

A brand-new account shows a customer that was never added: "Rohan Work / Never offered". Before deleting it, work out which of these it is — the answer decides how serious it is:

  • (a) A leftover seed/demo script inserting test data on account creation → remove the script and the row. Minor, done.
  • (b) Customers aren't scoped per account and this is another account's real contact → that is a data leak. Fix the scoping before anything else ships, then check what else isn't scoped.

"Rohan Work" looks like a real phone contact, which makes (b) uncomfortably plausible. Either way, tell Matt which it was.

Part 2 — Brand kit & design rules

The app is a dark navy system. These are the tokens and the rules that govern every screen.

2.1  Colours

TokenHexUsed for
Background navy#0B1A2EEvery screen's background
Surface#122540Cards, sheets, inputs
Money green#3DD68CMoney only — £ figures, the ring's payout segment — plus the small credential tick. Nothing else, ever.
Blue#5FA3F0Links, info chips, active tab tint, live-count chips
Amber—Pending / waiting states (Gas Safe check, Stripe needs info)
Red—Genuinely broken or needs-you (overdue, paused, banned, count badges)
White#FFFFFFPrimary buttons — the signature. One white primary per screen.

LAW Green is money. If a thing isn't a £ figure, the ring's payout segment, or the credential tick, it isn't green. (This is why the AUTO·SMS chip on Reminders is blue, list ticks are white, and the WhatsApp button is a white primary — see the NOTE list below.)

LAW Sentence case everywhere. Plain trade English — write for a van, not a boardroom. The wording blocklist (Part 18) applies to everything a customer could ever see. "Doorstep" stays banned in app copy.

2.2  The logo system

Three marks, three jobs — the wordmark introduces, the ring identifies, the seal vouches.

  • Wordmark — camel-case "TradeSura", "Trade" white / "Sura" blue. The logo. Leads on the welcome screen and letters.
  • Sura ring — the open circle completed by a green segment. App icon, favicon, avatar mark — and inside the app it doubles as the payout progress indicator (Part 6.3). Always place the supplied PNG/SVG — never redraw it as a plain circle.
  • Verified Member seal — the customer-facing credential (vans, leaflets, claim page). See the warning in 2.3.
  • In-app masthead = ring + wordmark lockup, exact asset, top-left of every tab screen.

2.3  One broken asset — don't ship it

The Verified Member seal PNG is concept-only. Its bottom arc text is mirrored — it literally reads "REBMEM DEIFIREV". Use it to understand the design direction and nothing else. A proper vector rebuild is with the designer; nothing prints or ships wearing the seal until that lands (this gates member-pack production, not your app work).

2.4  NOTE Picture-vs-build differences (standing list)

The target pictures were AI-generated. They're the truth for layout and copy, but they carry a few repeated slips. In the build:

  • Green hue — some pictures run a lime-ish green; the token is #3DD68C.
  • The ring — some pictures draw a plain circle; always place the real ring asset.
  • Ticks — the small green tick belongs to the credential line only ("Gas Safe verified"). Plan-benefit list ticks are white, even where a picture shows them green (the public page and route 1 pictures do).
  • Bell badge and lit tabs — pictures sometimes show the Reminders bell lit or badged on the wrong screen. These are data-driven states, not fixed pixels: badge only when items are due, lit only when it's the active tab.
  • Icons — one native family (SF Symbols), consistent line weight. No emoji as icons.
  • Pushed-page titles — left-aligned beside the back arrow (a couple of pictures centre them).
  • Status bars in pictures (times, "◀ TestFlight") are artefacts — ignore.
  • Avatar initials — should read "MW" (first + last name), not the email's first letter as today.
  • Old logo — the sign-in and signup pictures wear the retired "TRADESURA ✓" mark; build every header with the final ring lockup.

Part 3 — How the app is laid out

LAW The whole map is five tabs + four quick actions + one hero + one avatar. No Plans tab, no More tab.

  • Tab bar: Home · Customers · Add customer (the labelled hero: white circle, person-plus icon, label beneath — the bar's only filled element) · Reminders · Payouts. Blue tint for the active tab, labels kept.
  • Reminders bell wears a red count badge only when items are due this week or overdue. Zero items = no badge. (Red count badges are a system convention — the one place red doesn't mean broken.)
  • Header on tab screens: the lockup masthead left, avatar right ("MW" initials, small green tick badge once verified).
  • Pushed pages: back arrow + title (sentence case, left-aligned) instead of the masthead — and the tab bar stays, with the parent tab lit. Inside My plans, Home is lit; tapping Home pops back to the dashboard.
  • Avatar → Account page (Part 13). The route already exists — the avatar is wired to the old "More" screen today; the room gets rebuilt, not re-routed.
  • LAW Rooms are never locked; actions are. Every tab opens to an honest empty state in every account state. Gating happens on buttons, with a reason and a route (Part 6.5).

Part 4 — Getting in: onboarding

The pre-account journey: welcome → sign-in / create account → three signup steps → a once-ever "building your account" moment → the Getting Started hub. The fixes from the Onboarding Review (6 Sept) all still stand; the pictures below are the targets.

  • Signup must persist — the 1 Sept bug where profile details vanished after signup stays fixed and proven.
  • Referral code and claim links pre-fill their fields (attribution capture).
  • Duplicate Gas Safe number gets a friendly handled state, not a crash.

Part 5 — The Getting Started hub

Where every new account lands. Wiring (the P0 from Part 1.2):

  • Set up payments → Stripe onboarding (already works; see Part 17.1 for the popup fix).
  • Build my plan → the plan wizard (Part 8) in setup dress — a "Back to setup" bar, same flow.
  • Import customers → the Customers import flow (CSV / contacts).
  • Send my pack → address capture (the shared PAF lookup, Part 17.3) + the order queues. Address is allowed before verification; shipment only fires on badge-granted (Part 6.4). The line under the button says it plainly: "Ships when your badge goes live."
  • How TradeSura works → the How it works page (Part 14).
  • Skip setup for now → the dashboard in its skipped-setup state (works today — keep it).

Steps show done/undone state; the dashboard's "Finish setup — N of 4 done" card reads the same truth.

Part 6 — Home dashboard

6.1  Structure, top to bottom LAW

Header → greeting → standing strip → money card → action card → Today → quick actions → tab bar. The money card is position one: nothing may appear above it except the header, greeting and the slim standing strip — never another card, never anything that pushes the figure down.

6.2  The money card LAW

  • One hero number. Inactive: £0/month + "Your first plan changes this". Active: the monthly figure + a state-aware sub-line ("8 plans live · 2 offers out"). Nothing else ever lives on this card.
  • Headline money app-wide is the engineer's 80%. Processing pennies appear in exactly one place — Payouts' transparency card.

6.3  The ring LAW

  • Present from day one, dormant: the whole mark — green segment included — at ~35% opacity, static, captioned "PAID EVERY / Friday". NOTE The skipped-setup picture shows the green segment at full strength; dormancy is one opacity on the whole mark.
  • Wakes with the first live plan: full colour, caption flips to "NEXT PAYOUT / Friday · £X", and the ring fills through the payout week, closing green on Friday. Installers will learn: ring closing = money coming.
  • Payout maths: NEXT PAYOUT = that Friday's actual clearing amount — this week's confirmed collections × 80%. Never the monthly figure × 80%.

6.4  The standing strip LAW

The banner slot under the greeting is permanent infrastructure: one component, states as data, visible even when everything is healthy. Every state is tappable through to the Account status row. One strip only — when several things are true, the priority ladder is banned > paused > Stripe-needs-info > check-failed > check-pending > active. Payouts' banner reads this same truth source, and so does every verification string in the app — one vocabulary everywhere.

StateLookText
Check pendingAmber, clock iconGas Safe check in progress — we'll text you within 24 hours.
Check failedAmber, alert iconWe couldn't verify your Gas Safe number — check it and try again →
ActiveQuietest in the family: small green tick, muted grey text — the text itself is never greenGas Safe verified — account active.
PausedRedReason + "Fix it →"
BannedRedReason + WhatsApp support route

Badge-granted is one event with four effects: push notification ("You're Gas Safe verified — your member pack is on its way") → strip flips to quiet active → avatar gets its tick → member-pack shipment fires (Part 17.4).

6.5  Quick actions + gating

The 2×2 row: My plans · Invite an engineer — earn £50 · How it works · Membership Shop. Outlined cards, real icons.

LAW The soft-gate pattern. Gated things stay visible, muted and tappable — the tap opens a short sheet with the reason and the route back. Never hidden, never silently dead.

SurfaceInactive accountTap givesWakes when
My plansGreyedYour first plan is step 2 of setup — Continue setup →First plan live
Membership ShopGreyedThe shop unlocks with your badge — your free pack ships when it goes live.Badge live
Add customer heroGreyed (white circle + label drop to muted — still the bar's centrepiece, visibly asleep)Add customers once your first plan is live — Continue setup →First plan live
Invite an engineer / How it worksNever gated — full brightness always.

LAW The two-leg gate. Anything customer-facing — sending an offer, the show-my-plans flow — needs a live plan AND the badge. Today's build checks plan-only; add the badge leg. Inside the woken Add-customer sheet, routes 1–2 stay gated by both legs; route 3 (save details) opens as soon as the hero wakes.

6.6  The rest of the dashboard

  • Greeting sub-line is state-aware. Setup: "Once you're set up, offering a plan takes under 90 seconds." Active: "Offer a plan at the end of the job — most take under 90 seconds."
  • Action card cycles: Finish setup ("2 of 4 done" + Continue setup) → first customer → next best action. No two cards claim "first" at once.
  • Offers-waiting card (active state): kept, with a throttle. The nudge appears ~48 hours after the original offer text and fires once per offer, ever — then that offer goes quiet. The card is a state, not furniture: at zero it cycles to the next best action. Never render "0 offers waiting".
  • Today feed: honest per state. Setup state shows exactly "Nothing needs you today — no active plans or messages." and the box renders as a slim card until content exists. Red OVERDUE chips are legitimate red. "View all" routes to the Reminders tab. New-signup wins are a Home-only garnish.

Part 7 — My plans: the plan system

7.1  The model LAW

Plans are listings, built from a TradeSura-approved option library. The engineer picks what's included; TradeSura owns the words.

  • The option library lives server-side — TradeSura adds or edits options without an app release. Each option carries fixed, legally-vetted wording (name + one-line description) and flags set by TradeSura, including a required flag (required options render pre-ticked and unremovable in the wizard). CONFIG Which options carry the flag, and the final library contents, are Matt's calls — ship the mechanism.
  • The plan title is the only free text anywhere, and it runs the wording blocklist live (Part 18). Nothing customer-facing exists outside the versioned registry — that's what keeps every plan a maintenance contract, never insurance.
  • "No call-out fee" as a benefit is intentional — waiving a fee is a continuous-service benefit; we never promise to fix things. Don't "fix" it.
  • The old three templates (Boiler Care £12 / + Controls £15 / Landlord £15) become quick starts — pre-filled wizard runs. CONFIG Whether they show at launch is Matt's call; build the wizard so pre-fill is possible.
  • Price rails: £8–£25, £1 steps.

7.2  Versioning — what a customer signed is frozen LAW

  • Every signup pins to the exact version agreed — price, benefits, wording — frozen forever. Live Direct Debit amounts never change.
  • Any edit to a live plan (price or contents) creates a new version that applies to new customers only. The editor says so: "Changes apply to new customers — your N current customers keep what they signed up for."
  • Stop offering / Start offering again is one reversible toggle (no separate "paused" state). Stopping retires the plan from the public page and offers; live customers are untouched; the card chip flips to "Stopped · N still on this plan".
  • Delete exists only for drafts that never went live. A plan that ever had a customer can be stopped, never deleted.
  • The customer detail screen must show the version they signed (Part 10), not the current one.

7.3  Routing — there is no empty plans page LAW

  • Zero plans → every door opens the wizard directly. No empty My plans screen exists; don't build one.
  • First plan live → every door lands on the hub page, forever after. The hub is earned by the first plan.
  • The five doors (all → this one room): setup's Build my plan · dashboard quick action · Account row · the Add-customer sheet's Manage plans link · the offer gate's "Build my plan →".

7.4  The hub page and the editor

  • Card anatomy: title · £X/month (green) · keep-line "You keep £X.XX a month per customer." · the included lines · status chip (Live · N customers blue / Stopped · N still on this plan grey / Draft grey outline) · two outlined buttons: Edit plan · View customers.
  • View customers opens the Customers tab filtered to that plan — a deep link with the filter set, no new screen.
  • Tapping the card body does nothing (Matt's call). The chip is a status read; the buttons do the work.
  • Stopping asks once (a small confirmation sheet — plain words: live customers keep their plan; you can start offering again any time), then the card wears its Stopped face with a Start offering again button.

Part 8 — The plan wizard (four steps)

  • Step 1: checklist from the server-side library, each option with its fixed one-line description. Required-flagged options come pre-ticked and unremovable, worn as "included in every TradeSura plan". Counter: "3 selected — plans read best with 3 to 6."
  • Step 2: − / + stepper, £1 steps, clamped £8–£25. Keep-line recalculates live: "You keep £X.XX a month per customer." Quiet anchor: "Your plan, your price — most sit between £10 and £15."
  • Step 3: title field, ~28-character cap. Live blocklist with a friendly reason when it fires (Part 16). Suggested-name chips built from the Step 1 selections.
  • Step 4: shows the exact customer-facing card as it will appear on the public page and in offers — "This is exactly what customers will see." One white button: Make this plan live. Lands back on the hub with the card present. This tap is literally the gate's plan-exists leg switching on.
  • Back exits freely before Step 4 — nothing is committed until Make this plan live. Exiting after real input offers keep-as-draft (Draft chip on the hub).
  • Setup's Build my plan opens this same flow with a "Back to setup" bar. One builder, every door.
  • Persistence is this room's own acceptance test: create a plan → kill the app → reopen → the plan is there.

Part 9 — Add customer: the sheet and its three routes

Per-route gating: routes 1 and 2 need the two-leg gate (live plan AND badge). Route 3 opens as soon as the hero wakes (first plan live).

9.1  Route 1 — "They're with me — show my plans"

  • This is the in-person sales flow's only home. Tapping it flips the phone into customer mode: trust block (ring + trading name + "Gas Safe verified · Backed by TradeSura"), "Choose your plan", the live plan cards — the same card component as wizard Step 4 and the public page.
  • "Choose this plan" → the shared checkout (Part 15.2) — one checkout behind every door.
  • Signups through this route are auto-tagged in-person.
  • The ✕ asks nothing — it just hands the phone back to the engineer's app.

9.2  Route 2 — "Text them the offer"

  • The message is built server-side from a template — name-stamped, benefits pulled from the plan, and a per-customer link ("her link is hers alone"): it opens the public page with that plan pinned and her details pre-filled at checkout.
  • The engineer can change the recipient and the plan, not the words.
  • Send arms the 48-hour nudge clock for the dashboard's offers-waiting card (Part 6.6) — one nudge per offer, ever.

9.3  Route 3 — "Just save their details"

  • Name · mobile · address — the address field is the shared PAF lookup's first appearance (Part 17.3): postcode → Find address → picker → editable fill, manual fallback.
  • Last boiler service (optional) — a month picker. This date feeds the 30/14/3 reminder engine directly (Part 11); the helper line says so: "Powers automatic service reminders."
  • Save de-dupes by phone number against the existing book.

Part 10 — The Customers book

  • Filters: All · On plan · Not on plan · Payment issues (with counts). The old ⚠ icon-only pill fails van English — it wears its label.
  • The Offer button appears only on never-offered rows — the one-nudge law extends here: someone already offered doesn't get a second button, the 48h nudge machinery covers them. Status lines: "Never offered" · "Offered N days ago" · "{Plan} — joined this week" · "{Plan} — since {month}".
  • The bulk button texts the offer to everyone never-offered ("Text the offer to N customers") — doctrine naming, same verb as route 2.
  • "Add a customer by hand" link → the route 3 form. Import can't be the only way in.
  • Import your book (CSV / phone contacts) keeps the own-customers PECR checkbox — unverified since 1 Sept; confirm it exists — and de-dupes by phone automatically.
  • Customer detail: name + plan chip · "Her plan — as signed" card showing the signed version (title, price, benefits — frozen snapshot, Part 7.2; use the customer's pronoun where known, else "Their plan — as signed") · Service card (Last service / Next due with a red OVERDUE chip when late / white Mark service done button — tapping it resets the service clock and the reminder engine) · Contact card · Text the manage link at the bottom.
  • LAW There is no engineer-side cancel button. Cancellation lives only behind the customer's manage link — so every cancellation is provably customer-made. The engineer's tool is "Text the manage link".

Part 11 — Reminders

  • The engine: service texts go out automatically 30, 14 and 3 days before due. Plan customers get "book your included service"; reply-to-book as built. The due date comes from Mark service done, the saved last-service date, or import data.
  • Rows show what the machine did or will do ("Reminder sent — she can reply to book." / "3-day text goes out Tuesday."). Tapping a row opens that customer's detail, where Mark service done lives — the footer line says so.
  • The week strip stays compact; it earns more size only with content.
  • Notifications: tab count-badge (red) = due this week + overdue, zero = no badge · push permission is asked after the first plan goes live, with the pre-prompt "Get told when payouts land and services come due" · the app-icon badge mirrors overdue only.

Part 12 — Payouts

  • Hero: NEXT PAYOUT · £X (green) · Friday, with the ring beside it filling through the payout week (Part 6.3). Sub-line: "This week's cleared collections — your 80%, paid direct to your bank."
  • The transparency card is the only place processing costs exist, and the maths must reconcile to the penny: collections × 80% − processing = to your bank. Costs render neutral — never red; costs aren't errors.
  • Failed collection recovery: smart retries run automatically; the card reports plainly ("No failed collections in the last 30 days.").
  • Tax-year export (CSV) stays.
  • Before anything's live (no picture — build from words): same room, hero shows the empty-state line "Payouts start when your first plan goes live — paid every Friday.", dormant ring, transparency card at zeros.
  • If Stripe needs more information: an amber slim banner, tappable into the Stripe flow — it reads the standing strip's truth source. Red stays reserved for genuinely broken.

Part 13 — Account

  • Identity header: initials avatar (with the tick once verified), name, email.
  • Status card reads the standing strip's truth source — same words, same state machine: "Gas Safe verified — account active." / "Payments — active, paid every Friday." (amber variants + routes while pending).
  • Your business: trading name · Your page — the public address, derived from the trading name with a neutral fallback, never the email local-part (today's /p/info/… is the bug; the target is tradesura.com/p/mattwood) · logo (upload, not URL).
  • Four rows, each with a chevron: "My plans" — "Invite an engineer · £50" — "WhatsApp support" — "Terms & privacy". Then a muted Sign out.
  • Cut from the old More screen: the "This month, transparently" card (Payouts owns the money — one money room) · "Payouts & collections" row (duplicates the tab) · "How to sell more plans" (its content lives in How it works — one home). Hidden for October: "Messages & tickets" and "Trades & TradePacks" — unless one is load-bearing, in which case say what it does before it stays.

Part 14 — Invite an engineer · How it works · Membership Shop

  • RULED The £50 pays when the invited engineer's first plan goes live. (This closes the old first-plan-vs-five-plans question — the Refer screen's old "5 plans live" copy is superseded; the page is named "Invite an engineer" everywhere.) Keep the payout trigger a config value internally, but the shipped answer is first plan live, paid into the next Friday payout.
  • The referral ladder per invitee: Signed up → Verified → Plan live → £50 paid. Flat £50, no limit, no ongoing cut; self-referrals and same-household gaming are voided (the deal card says all this plainly — keep its words).
  • Sharing: WhatsApp invite (white primary button — not green), QR + copy link, and Share my income card — soft-gated ("Unlocks with your first payout") until there's a real card to share.
  • How it works absorbs the old "How to sell more plans": how you get paid, the maths, and the word-for-word script. It's the never-gated help room.
  • Membership Shop: the October face is the coming-soon card — "your free member pack ships when your badge goes live." LAW The credential lock is permanent: anything bearing the Verified Member seal can never be bought or shipped to an unverified account, and re-locks on pause or ban. Non-seal stock can open to any active account later.

Part 15 — The customer's side

Two web pages, no app chrome, no tab bar — and no green anywhere except the prices. The customer never sees the money machinery; she sees a deal and a trusted trade.

15.1  The public page

  • Address: tradesura.com/p/{trading-name-slug}. Header: ring + trading name + the trust line "Gas Safe verified · Backed by TradeSura". Title "Choose your plan", sub-line "Cancel anytime — set up takes about a minute." Then the live plan cards — same component as wizard Step 4 and route 1 — each with a white "Choose this plan". Footer: "Powered by TradeSura · Terms & privacy".
  • A personal offer link (route 2's per-customer link) pins the offered plan first with a one-line greeting — "{Engineer first name} suggested {Plan}" — and pre-fills her details at checkout. The generic address / QR shows all live plans, nothing pre-filled.
  • Only live plans appear. Stopped and draft plans never render here.
  • CONFIG What this page is called in app copy ("your TradeSura page" is the front-runner) — keep its strings in one place for a rename sweep.

15.2  The shared checkout

  • Title "Set up your plan", sub-line "{Plan} · £{X} a month · with {Trading name}". Her details (pre-filled from a personal link; typed fresh in the hand-the-phone flow — with the PAF lookup on the address). Then the Direct Debit card: account holder, sort code, account number, and the required line "Protected by the Direct Debit Guarantee." — Bacs rules want that visible at signup, and it stays.
  • The pending line (replaces the picture's stale date): Your Direct Debit takes 2–3 days to set up. First payment as soon as your Direct Debit is live — we'll text you before it's taken.
  • One white button: Set up my plan. Footer: "Cancel anytime. Powered by TradeSura · Terms & privacy".
  • LAW Billing is anniversary-based. The first collection happens as soon as the mandate is live, and then monthly on that date — Stripe's default subscription behaviour, nothing custom to build. No fixed calendar billing date exists anywhere.
  • After signup: welcome SMS to the customer, instant ping to the engineer, and the new row appears in his book and Today feed.
  • The manage link (magic link, no login): view plan, update details, cancel — reason chips, no dark patterns. This is the only cancel path in the product (Part 10).
  • NOTE Legal rider for Matt's terms drafting, not for you: "Cancel anytime" on screen means the terms must be rolling monthly, no minimum term, no exit fee. Flag anything that contradicts it.

Part 16 — Screens with no picture (build from words)

Everything here is deliberate spec-only — don't go hunting for renders that don't exist.

  • Greyed variants of the dashboard quick actions + the Add-customer hero, and their three gate sheets (words in Part 6.5).
  • Standing strip: check-failed, paused and banned states (Part 6.4's table).
  • Payouts before first payout — the empty face (Part 12).
  • Edit plan faces: the changed-state (versioning line showing) and the stopped face with "Start offering again"; plus the small stop-confirmation sheet (Part 7.4).
  • Wizard blocklist fired: the name field flags the word with a friendly reason — e.g. "That word can't go in a plan name — TradeSura plans are maintenance contracts, not insurance." — and Next stays disabled until it's gone.
  • Empty forms and pickers: route 3 blank, the month picker, the address picker states.
  • First-payout celebration — a one-time moment when the first real payout lands (design direction in Screen Designs v2). Small, joyful, once.
  • Offer-sent confirmation — route 2's after-state: a quiet toast/sheet ("Offer sent to {first name}"), landing back where he was.

Part 17 — Plumbing & integrations

17.1  Stripe in the app

  • Kill the iOS "wants to use stripe.com" popup: run Stripe onboarding in an ephemeral web session (no shared-cookie prompt). Loading state: "Opening Stripe" + animated blue dots.
  • Collections are Stripe subscriptions on Bacs — anniversary billing is the default; smart retries handle failures; advance-notice texts ride the SMS rail.
  • Payout maths everywhere reconciles to Stripe's records to the penny.

17.2  Stripe organisation

  • TradeSura Ltd's own Stripe account is live. Matt is inviting you as Developer + Sandbox Administrator — the invite is waiting on your email address, via Rohan; send it. Builds then move off your personal sandbox onto the TradeSura account. Matt keeps sole admin, configures Connect branding + the TRADESURA statement descriptor; live keys and the bank side stay with him until nearer launch.

17.3  Shared components

  • PAF address lookup — one shared component used everywhere an address appears (signup, pack order, route 3, checkout, and every future flow). Provider is your pick: getAddress / Ideal Postcodes / Loqate / Postcoder. API key server-side. Acceptance: type "HD9 3XF" → Find address → pick → fields fill, with a manual fallback.
  • The option library — server-side, versioned, with per-option flags (Part 7.1). Nothing customer-facing renders from outside it.
  • The standing-strip state machine — one truth source read by the strip, Payouts' banner, and the Account status card.

17.4  Member pack

  • Address capture is allowed pre-verification; the order queues. Shipment fires only on badge-granted (the Part 6.4 trigger chain). Fulfilment: local printer, batched. (Physical production also waits on the seal rebuild — Part 2.3.)

17.5  Store enrolment

  • Apple + Google under TradeSura Ltd (not 302 MD); Apple ID info@tradesura.com; Apple support case 102955530602 is open on Matt's side.

Part 20 — How you'll know it's finished

One walk on Matt's phone, end to end, no hands on the wheel:

  • 1. Create a plan in the wizard → kill the app → reopen → the plan is still there.
  • 2. An unverified account tries to send an offer → correctly held by the two-leg gate, with a working "Build my plan →" / verification route.
  • 3. A verified sandbox account sends an offer → the text arrives → her personal link opens the public page with the plan pinned → sandbox Bacs checkout completes → welcome flow fires.
  • 4. The dashboard money card, Customers, Reminders and Payouts all update — and the payout maths shows the week's clearing × 80%, reconciling to the penny.
  • 5. The phantom customer is gone, with the answer to which bug it was.

When that walk works, the app is done in every way that matters — everything left is polish against the pictures in this guide.
